solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Supporters’ talk involving openings for youth team — what a surprise (5,4)

indicatorNotes.involving: the talk takes in, or involves, the letters inside it
indicatorNotes.openings for: the openings of words are their first letters

blocks.note: supporters are fans; talk is chat
first letters of youth and team

annotation.surface: Fans gossiping about the youth side, astonished at what they have heard.
annotation.walkthrough: YT goes in after the C of FAN CHAT, making FANC-YT-HAT.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: both phrases are exclamations a speaker uses on hearing something unexpected.

entries.clue: Passenger, first to depart, got on (5)

blocks.note: a taxi driver's passenger is a fare

annotation.surface: A traveller who was the first to leave the train had actually just boarded it.
annotation.walkthrough: "Got on" looks like boarding a vehicle, which suits the passenger; here it means managed, as in "How did you get on?"
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of managing: "how did you fare?" asks how you got on.

entries.clue: Fruit tree can supply nursing home (9)

indicatorNotes.supply: read as the adverb of supple: the letters of TREE CAN bend into a new shape
indicatorNotes.nursing: the rearranged letters hold IN as a nurse holds a baby

annotation.surface: A fruit tree might provide produce for a care home.
annotation.walkthrough: "Supply" looks like a verb, but it is the adverb from supple, meaning flexibly, and the nursing home is just the word home.
annotation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned kind of peach.

entries.clue: Agreed to accept caution, leaving with very strong feelings (9)

indicatorNotes.to accept: YES takes in the other letters
indicatorNotes.leaving: the W for with goes away from WARNING

blocks.note: caution is a warning; W is the abbreviation for with, and it leaves

annotation.surface: Someone accepted a formal caution and walked out seething.
annotation.walkthrough: W is the standard abbreviation for with, so "leaving with" drops the W from WARNING.
annotation.definitionFit: Yearnings are intense longings, strong feelings of desire.

entries.clue: Flag device from horror studio with stomach-turning real gore at the end (6,3,6)

indicatorNotes.at the end: take the end letter of each of real and gore

blocks.note: Hammer Films, the British studio famous for horror
last letters of real and gore

annotation.surface: A horror film studio's logo drawn from truly revolting bloodshed.
annotation.walkthrough: Hammer was a British film company famous for its horror films. The device is the emblem on the old Soviet flag.
annotation.definitionFit: The crossed hammer and sickle is the emblem on the Soviet flag.

entries.clue: Eliot, Cromwell, as well as Hotspur: no one exceptional? (3,4,3,5)

blocks.note: the poet T. S. Eliot was Tom
Richard Cromwell, Oliver's son, was mocked as Tumbledown Dick

annotation.surface: A question whether three famous historical Englishmen were really ordinary after all.
annotation.walkthrough: The Cromwell is Richard, not Oliver, and Hotspur is Sir Henry (Harry) Percy of Shakespeare's Henry IV. "Every Tom, Dick and Harry" means just anybody.
annotation.definitionFit: Tom, Dick and Harry means ordinary people, nobody in particular.

entries.clue: Bear with recurrent bad cough (5)

indicatorNotes.recurrent: running back, so the bear's name is written backwards

annotation.surface: A bear suffering from a hacking cough that keeps coming back.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bear" looks like the verb, to put up with, but it is Pooh; "recurrent" looks like it describes the cough.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the gasping intake of breath is the symptom that names whooping cough.

entries.clue: More sensible of Scrooge for one to flip character at the start (5)

indicators: to flip character at the start

indicatorNotes.to flip character at the start: turn the first letter upside down: M becomes W

annotation.surface: Scrooge might have been wiser to change his character early on.
annotation.walkthrough: The flip is physical: an M turned over is a W.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are comparatives of having good judgement.

entries.clue: Observable, with the passage of time (5)

annotation.surface: Something becomes visible as time goes by.
annotation.walkthrough: "Over time" means with the passage of time, so the wordplay reads straight off the phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: Overt means open, plainly observable.

entries.clue: Colonnade steeply raked: I run up through it (9)

indicatorNotes.raked: the letters of steeply are raked over into a new order
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means written backwards
indicatorNotes.through: the reversed pair goes through the rearranged letters

blocks.note: R is short for run, as in cricket scores

annotation.surface: A steep colonnade, and the speaker runs up through it.
annotation.walkthrough: "Raked" suggests a sloping stage or seating, which fits steeply; it means raked over, mixed up.
annotation.definitionFit: A peristyle is a row of columns surrounding a courtyard or building.

entries.clue: Recover two cities inside border (7)

indicatorNotes.inside: the two cities go inside the border

blocks.note: EC, the City of London postcode, and LA, Los Angeles

annotation.surface: Taking back two frontier cities.
annotation.walkthrough: EC is the postcode for the City of London, a favourite crossword city.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean getting back what was lost or taken.

entries.clue: Wrongly pick up circulating cash to clip (7)

blocks.note: M1, the money supply measure of notes, coins and current accounts, read as MI

annotation.surface: Someone mistakenly collects the cash that is going round in order to trim it.
annotation.walkthrough: M1 is the economists' name for the money in circulation; the digit 1 is read as the letter I. "Pick up" means catch by ear.
annotation.definitionFit: Pick up is used in its hearing sense, as in catching a remark, so doing it wrongly is the answer.

entries.clue: Attracted by river in early light (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the river goes in the early light

annotation.surface: Someone was lured to a river at daybreak.
annotation.walkthrough: R sits inside DAWN after the D: D-R-AWN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: being pulled towards someone or something.

entries.clue: Goes for good record label with good prices (9)

blocks.note: G is short for good; rates are prices

annotation.surface: A record label's good prices draw someone in.
annotation.walkthrough: "Good" appears twice: in the definition it means forever, and in the wordplay it is just G.
annotation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's country, going for good.

entries.clue: Abdicate, not having succeeded in this? (5)

annotation.definition: Abdicate, not having succeeded in this?

indicatorNotes.not having: the word is without S, the abbreviation for succeeded

blocks.note: to abdicate is to resign the throne
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded, and it is removed

annotation.surface: A monarch who quits without managing to rule at all.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a monarch who abdicates gives up the reign, perhaps having had little success in it.
annotation.definitionFit: A reign is what a monarch has and what abdicating ends.

entries.clue: Salesman daily travelling around quietly free to return (5-4)

indicatorNotes.travelling: the letters of daily move about
indicatorNotes.around: the rearranged letters go around P

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative
P, piano, is quiet in music

annotation.surface: A travelling salesman does his rounds every day, quietly free to head home.
annotation.walkthrough: P goes inside the rearranged DAILY: LY-P-AID.
annotation.definitionFit: A reply-paid envelope has its postage paid, so it is free to send back.

entries.clue: Where patient may be likely to lose guts after a week, in clumsy way (9)

indicatorNotes.to lose guts: likely loses its insides, leaving only its outer letters
indicatorNotes.after: the rest comes after A WK

annotation.surface: A patient is likely to be disembowelled after a week in hospital, done ham-fistedly.
annotation.walkthrough: "Lose guts" sounds like surgery, which suits the patient; it just empties likely to LY.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: awkward and clumsy both describe ungainly movement, and -ly matches "in ... way".

entries.clue: A new suggestion regarding first course (9)

annotation.surface: A fresh idea about how to start a meal or a series of lessons.
annotation.walkthrough: "First course" could be a first lesson; here it is the first dish of a meal.
annotation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian starter, the first course of a meal.

entries.clue: For heroic deeds, Wagner’s operas satisfy (7-2)

blocks.note: Der Ring des Nibelungen, Wagner's four-opera cycle

annotation.surface: Wagner's operas fit the bill when it comes to heroics.
annotation.walkthrough: Wagner's Ring cycle is often called just Der Ring, which supplies the whole first word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from a Middle English phrase meaning daring to do, now used for bold, swashbuckling exploits.

entries.clue: Advanced with vigour and ripped dress open (7,2)

indicatorNotes.ripped: a ripped dress is torn apart, as its letters are

annotation.surface: Someone charged forward so energetically that their dress tore open.
annotation.walkthrough: "Ripped" looks like part of the story of a torn dress; it tells you to rearrange the next two words.
annotation.definitionFit: To press on is to keep advancing determinedly.

entries.clue: Half portion of pasta and cake (5)

indicatorNotes.Half portion of: take half the letters of the pasta

blocks.note: its first five of ten letters

annotation.surface: Half a helping of pasta followed by cake.
annotation.walkthrough: The pasta has to be guessed: TORTELLINI has ten letters, and its first half is the cake.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the German torte is one kind of rich, layered cake.

entries.clue: Jaundiced, you will want to accept nothing (9)

indicatorNotes.to accept: the words take nothing in between them

blocks.note: ye'll, an old way of saying you will

annotation.surface: A cynic will always want to take nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: "Jaundiced" usually means cynical, which suits the surface; here it is literal, the yellow skin of jaundice.
annotation.definitionFit: Jaundice turns the skin yellowish.

entries.clue: Source of rubber in recent times (5)

annotation.surface: Where rubber has come from lately.
annotation.walkthrough: "Times" is the multiplication sign X, not a period.
annotation.definitionFit: Latex is the milky sap of rubber trees.

entries.clue: Recombine elements of very lightweight gas (5)

indicatorNotes.Recombine elements of: put the parts back together in the other order

blocks.note: a single ounce weighs very little; recombined, the unit comes first and the number second

annotation.surface: Chemistry: rearranging the atoms of a very light gas.
annotation.walkthrough: The chemistry is misdirection: the elements are the two words of ONE OZ, which change places. Ozone is indeed recombined oxygen atoms.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: ozone is one particular gas, three oxygen atoms bonded together.

entries.clue: Tight-lipped about son that creates a range of colours (5)

annotation.definition: that creates a range of colours
annotation.definitionNote: a relative clause standing for the noun: something that creates a range of colours

indicatorNotes.about: about in its sense of around, so PRIM surrounds the son

annotation.surface: A strait-laced parent whose son is a colourful character.
annotation.walkthrough: S sits inside PRIM: PRI-S-M.
annotation.definitionFit: A prism splits white light into a spectrum of colours.

entries.clue: Has to finish off pastry smelling stale (5)

annotation.surface: Someone is obliged to eat up the stale-smelling pastry.
annotation.walkthrough: "Finish off" suggests eating the pastry up; it only takes its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the damp, mouldy smell of a closed room.

entries.clue: Illustrations of couple beginning to relax in boat (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the pieces go in the boat

annotation.surface: Pictures of two people starting to unwind in a boat.
annotation.walkthrough: The couple and the boat hint at Noah's animals boarding two by two.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in publishing, where the pictures in a book are collectively its artwork.

entries.clue: Polymers holding last of rotting steps down (7)

indicatorNotes.holding: the polymers hold the letter inside

annotation.surface: Plastic coating over rotting stair treads.
annotation.walkthrough: "Steps down" looks like part of the rotting staircase; it is the definition, meaning quits.
annotation.definitionFit: To resign is to step down from a post.

entries.clue: Fail to recruit team for Union opponents (5)

annotation.definitionNote: Dixie is the Confederate South, singular, standing for the states that fought the Union

indicatorNotes.to recruit: fail takes the team into its ranks

blocks.note: a cricket or football eleven, in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: A side that fails to sign new players for a match against the trade unionists.
annotation.walkthrough: "Union" looks like a trade union or rugby union; it is the Union side in the American Civil War.
annotation.definitionFit: Dixie is the American South, whose Confederate states fought the Union.

entries.clue: Gloomy yet surprisingly wordy study? (9)

indicatorNotes.surprisingly: the letters come out in an unexpected order

annotation.surface: A gloomy but unexpectedly verbose piece of research.
annotation.walkthrough: "Wordy" usually means verbose, but here it means about words, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Etymology is the study of where words come from.
